I found one bug in the uncommitted changes.

**`docs/service.py:38`: `rename` has no ownership check (authorization bypass).**
- `rename` calls `self.repo.get(doc_id)` directly. Every other operation (`read`, `update_body`, `delete`) goes through `self._owned(user_id, doc_id)`.
- `user_id` is never used in `rename`, so any user can rename any other user's document by passing its id.
- The ids of other users' documents are also exposed. A missing id raises `NotFound` from `repo.get`. An existing id belonging to someone else succeeds. That breaks the `_owned` docstring's promise that the API never reveals which ids exist.

Fix:
```python
document = self._owned(user_id, doc_id)
```
You could also move the call above the title validation. Then an unauthorized caller always gets `NotFound` and never a validation error for a document they don't own.

I didn't see any other issues in the diff. The title validation (strip, empty check, 200-character limit) looks fine.
